1B.4.note: Partially met, and the remaining gap is Go-only. STATIC TYPES are now clean in all six SDKs: optional OBJECT/REF/ARRAY and nullable-typed members preserve absence via Go pointers (*T / *[]T), TS optional chaining (?: T), Ruby nilable, Python NotRequired[T], Swift optionals (T?), and Kotlin nullable (T? = null). CORRECTION (2026-07-27): this entry previously claimed Kotlin emits optional non-array SCALARS with zero-value sentinels (Boolean = false, Int = 0, Long = 0L). That has been FALSE since #424 — zero such defaults exist in the generated Kotlin models. Kotlin also distinguishes the third wire state, required-and-nullable, as `T?` with NO default (vs `T? = null` for optional), so an omitted key still fails to decode. Both halves are now pinned by check-kotlin-optional-arrays-and-scalars, which since this correction covers primitive scalars as well as arrays (object/$ref/enum members stay out of scope — they are reference types with no sentinel to guard). REMAINING GAP (why pass stays false): runtime round-trip, not static types. Go optional NON-POINTER scalars collapse absence on DECODE (an absent field and an explicit zero both unmarshal to the zero value); only Go pointer fields (*T) preserve it. Ruby/Swift decode faithfully but drop nil on RE-ENCODE (compact / synthesized encoder). Resolving the Go half is a per-schema question answerable via the existing x-go-type-skip-optional-pointer precedent; it must NOT be a blanket omitempty waiver, since a meaningful fraction of the affected fields are request-shaped and an explicit zero differs from absence on a write. Documented in SPEC.md §10 Optional Fields and tracked in #436. Go's *[]T is used only where rich-text projections need the wire distinction round-tripped both directions; not a blanket sweep.
